entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Jos 14:1-5 . The Nine Tribes and a Half to Have Their Inheritance by Lot.

entries.heading: 4. The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim
entries.text: 4. The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim --As two and a half tribes were settled on the east Jordan, and the Levites had no inheritance assigned them in land, there would have been only eight and a half tribes to provide for. But Ephraim and Manasseh, the two sons of Joseph, had been constituted two tribes ( Ge 48:5 ), and although Levi was excluded, the original number of the tribes of Israel was still preserved.

entries.heading: 5. the children of Israel . . . divided the land
entries.text: 5. the children of Israel . . . divided the land --that is, they made the preliminary arrangements for the work. A considerable time was requisite for the survey and measurement.

entries.heading: Verse 6
entries.text: Jos 14:6-15 . Caleb by Privilege Requests and Obtains Hebron.

entries.heading: 12. give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day
entries.text: 12. give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day --this highland region. for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there --The report of the spies, who tried to kindle the flame of sedition and discontent, related chiefly to the people and condition of this mountain district, and hence it was promised as the reward of Caleb's truth, piety, and faithfulness.

entries.heading: 13, 14. Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb Hebron for an inheritance
entries.text: 13, 14. Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb Hebron for an inheritance --Joshua, who was fully cognizant of all the circumstances, not only admitted the claim, but in a public and earnest manner prayed for the divine blessing to succor the efforts of Caleb in driving out the idolatrous occupiers.

entries.heading: 15. Kirjath-arba
entries.text: 15. Kirjath-arba --that is, the city of Arba, a warrior among the native race remarkable for strength and stature. the land had rest from war --Most of the kings having been slain and the natives dispirited, there was no general or systematic attempt to resist the progress and settlement of the Israelites.
